__comment: OAuth 1.0a (HMAC-SHA1) replaces any username/password validator. customUI hosts the consent webview (like com.palm.eas / com.palm.skype); getAuthorizeUrl runs OAuth leg 1 (request_token) and returns the authorize URL + request token/secret, Atlas captures oauth_verifier from the redirect to Config.CALLBACK_URL, then exchangeCode runs leg 3 (access_token) and returns the stored token credentials. Flickr is a PHOTO source only - no DOCUMENTS capability, no files app.

__comment3: com.palm.service.flickr is in read+writePermissions so the service itself can readCredentials(accountId) to sign photo-provider calls. Flickr OAuth 1.0a tokens do NOT expire/rotate, so writeCredentials is effectively unused after create (kept for symmetry).

capabilityProviders.__comment: The file-picker app and the account-derived QuickOffice reroute consume listFolder/downloadFile/uploadFile. Locators are absolute HiDrive paths under the account home; the root sentinel 'home' maps to /users/<user>.

Makes the HiDrive account a photo source. The Photos aggregator calls com.palm.service.hidrive/listAlbums+listPhotos; one folder ('Camera Uploads' under home) is surfaced as one album. src_big is a '/file?path=..&access_token=..' URL fetched by the aggregator's curl (see adapter.getTemporaryLink).

__comment: kDrive (Infomaniak) is TOKEN-based: the customUI app com.palm.app.kdrive-auth takes a personal API token (Drive scope) and calls verifyToken, which validates it and auto-discovers account_id + drive_id, returning credentials.common = {accessToken, accountId, driveId}. OAuth was ruled out - Infomaniak OAuth/OIDC only grants identity scopes and rejects `drive` (invalid_scope). validator.address points at verifyToken; the app derives the service URI from it. DOCUMENTS-only (no PHOTO.UPLOAD provider).
__comment2: com.palm.app.kdrive-auth MUST be in write/readPermissions: createAccount runs under the customUI auth app's identity and is permission-checked against these lists (accounts/handlers/create.js -> Utils.hasPermission).
__comment3: com.palm.service.kdrive is in read+writePermissions so the service can readCredentials(accountId) for file ops and writeCredentials back after an OAuth token refresh. Token-mode credentials are long-lived (no refresh).

capabilityProviders.__comment: The file-picker app (and the QuickOffice reroute) consume listFolder/downloadFile/uploadFile. kDrive is numeric-ID based (adapter stringifies ids for consumers); the drive-root id is 1 but is non-writable - the adapter resolves it to the private-space folder.

Makes the kDrive account a photo source. implementation/hooks point at the stock Photos AGGREGATOR (com.palm.service.photos), which discovers PHOTO.UPLOAD accounts and (via the templateId->serviceName switch in its Utils.js - see ../photos-integration/) calls com.palm.service.kdrive/listAlbums+listPhotos, then downloads bytes with the curl-patched Sync-Manager. One kDrive folder (Config.PHOTO_ALBUM_NAME, default 'Pictures', under the private-space root) is surfaced as one album; src_big/src_small carry ?access_token= (kDrive has no unauthenticated pre-signed links), so the curl -L fetch needs no auth header.

__comment: Mega has NO OAuth: sign-in is the account EMAIL + PASSWORD. The customUI app com.palm.app.mega-auth renders a two-field form and calls com.palm.service.mega/login, which runs the us0/us handshake and returns the stored session credentials. Unlike the OAuth connectors (shared com.palm.app.cloud-auth), Mega ships its own auth app. MEGA provides BOTH DOCUMENTS and PHOTO.UPLOAD (photo source + device->cloud upload).

capabilityProviders.__comment: The file-picker app and the QuickOffice reroute consume listFolder/downloadFile/uploadFile. The reroute is account-derived (FileStore routes ANY DOCUMENTS capability implemented by a palm://com.palm.service.* URI via the generic 'modern' path, keyed on account _id), so this needs NO per-provider mxId or QuickOffice change. Locators are opaque Mega node handles; the root sentinel 'root' maps to the Cloud Drive root.

Makes the MEGA account a photo source (and device->cloud upload target). The stock Photos aggregator (com.palm.service.photos) discovers PHOTO.UPLOAD accounts and - via the templateId->serviceName fall-through in its Utils.js (see ../photos-integration/) - calls com.palm.service.mega/listAlbums+listPhotos. One folder is surfaced as one album: 'Camera Uploads' under the Cloud Drive root. NOTE: Mega is end-to-end encrypted, so listPhotos DOWNLOADS+DECRYPTS each image to a local file and returns a file:// src_big (the aggregator's curl cannot decrypt Mega's ciphertext URLs).
